name: The Apologists (Defending the Faith)

objectives.text: Identify an apologist as a person who explains and defends what Christians believe
Name Justin Martyr as an early Christian teacher who wrote to explain the faith to rulers
Retell how early apologists answered false stories about Christians with truthful explanations and honest living
Explain from 1 Peter 3:15 that Christians are called to give a reason for their hope with gentleness and respect
Describe the charges of atheism, cannibalism, and disloyalty brought against Christians and how apologists explained Christian worship, the Lord's Supper, and prayer for rulers
Explain how Justin Martyr's First Apology addressed the emperor and asked that Christians be judged fairly rather than condemned for the name alone
Describe how Paul at the Areopagus began with what his hearers knew and pointed them to the Creator and the risen Christ as a model the apologists followed
Compare defending the faith by reasoned argument and godly conduct with defending it by force using examples from the apologists
Identify major early apologists such as Aristides, Justin, Athenagoras, Theophilus, Tertullian, and Origen along with the audiences they addressed
Describe how the Epistle to Diognetus presented the distinctive life of Christians as a witness to the truth of the faith
Analyze how Justin's Dialogue with Trypho used Old Testament prophecy to argue that Jesus is the promised Messiah
Explain how Justin used the Greek idea of the Logos to present Christ and compare his use with the teaching of John 1
Explain how the apologists argued from the created order to one Creator and relate their argument to the Reformed teaching on the light of nature
Analyze how Origen's Against Celsus answered educated pagan objections such as those against the incarnation and the resurrection
Analyze the structure of argument in Justin's First Apology including appeals to justice, moral life, fulfilled prophecy, and the description of Christian worship
Summarize the Rule of Faith as stated by Irenaeus and Tertullian and explain how apologists used it as a faithful summary of apostolic teaching
Evaluate the benefits and risks of the apologists' use of Greek philosophy by comparing Justin's approach with Tertullian's
Evaluate the apologists' arguments in light of the Reformed teaching that the authority of Scripture rests on God rather than on human proofs
Compare the methods of the early apologists with classical, evidential, and presuppositional approaches in modern apologetics
Create a written apology answering a contemporary objection to the Christian faith modeled on the method of an early apologist and grounded in Scripture

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (definition of apologist, Justin Martyr, accusations and responses, First Apology, Dialogue with Trypho, Logos, philosophy risks, modern connection). Dropped vague filler (words to defend Jesus, apply knowing why we believe). Recast swords vs truth as a grounded comparison. Removed Irenaeus versus Gnosticism as belonging to the Heresies sibling, and recast the Rule of Faith at grade 10 as apologetic summary rather than creedal development, which belongs to Councils and Creeds. Replaced the vague defense of rationality with a creative written apology. Added Acts 17 as model, the roster of apologists, Epistle to Diognetus, argument from creation tied to WCF 1.1, Origen against Celsus, and a Reformed evaluation of apologetics tied to WCF 1.4-1.5. Added verse-level Scripture anchors throughout.
